title: Earning halal
hook: Your paycheck can be worship too. Here's how to keep it clean.

screens.text: Most of your waking hours go to work or school. Islam doesn't treat that time as separate from your faith. Today: honest work, and the jobs worth asking about.
**Work is honorable.** The Prophet ﷺ said nobody eats better food than what they earned with their own hands, and that the Prophet **Dawud** (David) lived from his own labor [Bukhari 2072].
bubbles: With the right niyyah (intention), earning to support yourself and your family is a form of worship, whatever the job's status or pay [Revealed Path ch. 24].

Not quite. Earning with your own hands is praised [Bukhari 2072]. It's worship with the right intention.

screens.text: **Halal earning has two sides. First: how you work.** The Prophet ﷺ found wet grain hidden under dry grain at a market stall and said whoever cheats isn't one of us [Muslim 102].
bubbles: At work that means: honest timesheets, no fake sick days, no hiding a product's flaws, no padding the bill.

items.text: Logging the hours you actually worked
items.why: Honest timesheets are part of halal earning.

items.text: Calling in a fake sick day
items.why: That takes pay for a lie. Don't take people's money unjustly [Q 2:188].

items.text: Adding a few extra hours to a client's bill
items.why: Padding the bill is taking money unjustly [Q 2:188].

items.text: Charging a fair price for good work
items.why: Fair profit is halal. The problem is deception.

screens.prompt: Which of these breaks the Prophet's rule ﷺ about cheating?

options.text: Selling a used phone without mentioning the cracked battery
options.feedback: Right. Hiding a flaw is exactly the wet grain under the dry [Muslim 102].

options.text: Charging a fair price for good work
options.feedback: Not quite. Fair profit is halal. The problem is deception.

options.text: Turning down a sale you're not sure about
options.feedback: Not quite. Stepping back from something doubtful protects you [Bukhari 52].

screens.text: **Second: what the work is.** A job is a question when its main work is something Islam forbids. Some jobs are in between: ask [Bukhari 52]. Already in a job like this? Talk to your imam privately, soon.
bubbles: Selling or serving alcohol, or gambling [Q 5:90; Bukhari 2236].
{teen}If you're under 18: part-time jobs are great, like tutoring, babysitting, retail, lifeguarding or a grocery store.{/teen}
{teen}Before saying yes to a restaurant or store job, check whether you'd serve alcohol or handle pork, and ask {{mentor.name}} or your imam if so.{/teen}
{teen}Follow your parents' and your state's rules on teen work, and keep school first.{/teen}

screens.situation: Luis has served tables for three years. Part of his job is serving beer and wine. He just became Muslim, pays rent with this job, and feels sick about it.

options.text: Talk to his imam privately this week about his situation, and start looking for other work now
options.feedback: Yes. He takes it seriously without making a panicked choice alone. The imam can guide him on the timing.

options.text: Quit tonight with no plan and no savings
options.feedback: His heart's in the right place, but losing rent overnight can create new harm. Get guidance first, and quickly.

options.text: Decide it's fine since he doesn't drink it himself
options.feedback: Not quite. Serving it is part of the issue, not just drinking it. Don't settle it alone: ask the imam.

steps: Look at your job, school work or side hustle. Is there one small dishonest habit (a padded time, an excuse)?

screens.text: Honest work is worship. Don't cheat, don't take what isn't yours, and if your job's main work is something Islam forbids, ask your imam soon instead of deciding alone.
Clean money, earned honestly, carries blessing.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Earning by your own work is praised; Dawud lived from his labor [Bukhari 2072]. With a good intention, earning to support family is worship; any lawful, honest work is noble [Revealed Path ch. 24].
- Cheating is condemned [Muslim 102]; consuming others' wealth unjustly is forbidden [Q 2:188]. Employees should work with care; employers must pay fairly [Revealed Path ch. 24].
- Clearly forbidden fields: alcohol and gambling [Q 5:90]; trading in alcohol, pigs, carrion and idols [Bukhari 2236]; interest [Q 2:275–279]; fraud. Between clear halal and clear haram are doubtful matters; avoiding them protects your faith [Bukhari 52].
- Convert advice: keep your job and studies; don't blow up your life in the first months [Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices, V11].

**Likely questions**
- *"My job involves alcohol. Do I have to quit?"* (scholar question Q31) Don't rule on their case. Say: serving or selling alcohol isn't work to stay in long-term; talk to your imam privately this week; start looking for other work; don't make a panicked decision alone. Offer "Ask my imam."
- *"Bank job?"* Depends on the role (tellers, IT, loan officers differ). General picture: roles directly arranging interest are the clearest concern. Escalate for their role.
- *"Delivery apps?"* Generally ordinary work. If the app sends alcohol orders, that's a question for the imam.
- *"Stocks, 401(k)?"* General picture only: it depends on what the businesses do and whether interest is involved. Route their specific accounts to the imam; link Day 53. No financial advice beyond pointing to a professional.

**Escalate:** any convert currently in a job involving alcohol, gambling, interest, pork or adult content; business ownership questions; retirement accounts and existing debts (Q24 territory, Day 53).

**Don't**
- Don't tell anyone to quit immediately, or to stay.
- Don't give financial or legal advice; point to a professional.
- For teens: keep examples to student jobs; school and parents' rules come first.
